title: Israel among the empires
visualIdentity: Historical atlas extended with a chronology desk, categorical evidence matrix and documentary archive explorer; sage, copper and blue in the shared site typography.

interactionSequence.question: Who is subordinate to whom?
interactionSequence.method: Select a period; read both maps and the two political-status statements.
interactionSequence.outcome: Distinguish coalition, tribute, annexation, forced displacement and return.

interactionSequence.question: What changes when the scale changes?
interactionSequence.method: Compare regional relationships with named places in the southern Levant; switch between power and people.
interactionSequence.outcome: Separate a royal capital’s outcome from the experience of an entire population.

interactionSequence.question: What does a date actually date?
interactionSequence.method: Read the proportional time window and its explanation.
interactionSequence.outcome: Distinguish event, object, broad horizon and debated alignment.

interactionSequence.question: Whose victory in 701?
interactionSequence.method: Select event, payment and explanation comparisons.
interactionSequence.outcome: Locate overlap, discrepancies and theological interpretation without forced harmonization.

interactionSequence.question: Does a parallel restoration account prove Ezra’s decree?
interactionSequence.method: Choose and review an inference about the Cyrus Cylinder.
interactionSequence.outcome: Use comparative context without claiming direct attestation.

interactionSequence.question: What was actually consulted?
interactionSequence.method: Open the register and follow object and research links.
interactionSequence.outcome: Distinguish catalogue verification, primary translation, abstract and deeper reading.

states.heading: A campaign leaves a list, not a border.
An ally against Assyria becomes a tributary.
Protection and conquest can come from the same power.
The throne remains. The choice of king does not.
A kingdom ends. Its people have different futures.
Return does not restore the old kingdom.
The archive continues beyond the homecoming story.

verification.sourceAudit: 32 source records; expanded claim checks and bibliographic checks in companion dossier.
visualReview: Mobile expanded chronology and archive views
Selected witness matrix and scholarly disagreement layout
verification.sourceLinkCheck: All source IDs resolve; URL syntax and internal anchors checked. External records consulted during research; some primary sites reject direct automated retrieval, as recorded per source. No claim that every external endpoint returned HTTP 200.

finalAudit.research: Materially expanded with primary-object comparisons, selected original research and an explicit consultation ledger.
finalAudit.teaching: Evidence, inference and limits remain adjacent; archive selection and chronological methods are explained.
finalAudit.disagreement: Regional continuity and chronology are attributed and bounded; no invented consensus or population total.
finalAudit.visuals: Categorical matrix, schematic reasoning chains and an attributed proportional documentary span.
finalAudit.gaps: Documented in the companion dossier and exposed on the page.

limitations: Full modern editions of the Assyrian corpus would deepen philological comparison; no claim of full collation is made.
Karnak plates and uncertain toponyms need specialist study before any exact campaign map.
No attempt to estimate total numbers deported or returning from biased surviving samples.
Yehud’s changing provincial limits require dedicated regional research before territorial drawing.
Full archaeological reports and administrative editions remain deeper reading, not silently assimilated evidence.

expansion.politics: Three schematic authority relationships link directly to corresponding atlas periods.
expansion.chronology: Three cases distinguish object date, event date and reconstructed sequence; optional year-counting diagram.
expansion.witnesses: Three source types compared across four historical questions; each column opens observation, interpretation and limits.
expansion.archives: Three documentary settings; evidence first, optional inference, visible limits and a proportional family-attestation timeline.
expansion.debate: Destruction and rural continuity compared by evidence and method, followed by a 2021 archaeological reassessment.
expansion.scholarship: Seven annotated routes into editions, original research and historical arguments, with access status.
